questions.q: According to the summary, what did Nixon rely on to rise from his humble beginnings?
a: Hard work and consistency across many fields
Family wealth and political connections
Luck alone, without any preparation
A single talent he discovered early
questions.why: Lesson 1 says his varied experience in law, the Navy and politics positioned him so that opportunity could find him.

questions.q: What happened to Nixon's family life as his career advanced?
a: He drifted away from his wife and daughters
He retired early to spend time with them
He moved them happily into the White House
He gave up politics to protect them
questions.why: Lesson 2 says his family felt him growing distant while his involvement in politics only increased.

questions.q: What did Nixon's paranoia and heavy drinking lead to, per the summary?
a: A dark path away from his principles and family
Greater popularity with the press
A decision to resign before Watergate
A new focus on domestic policy
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes paranoiac episodes and a drift from his family and values, driven by substance and alcohol use.

questions.q: What was Watergate in the summary?
a: A break-in by Nixon's team that unraveled his presidency
A treaty Nixon signed with China
A newspaper that supported his campaign
A speech that won him the 1972 election
questions.why: Lesson 3 recounts his team breaking into the Democrats' Watergate offices and the investigations that followed.

questions.q: How did the Watergate investigation finally end Nixon's mandate?
a: Leaked information and tapes proved his involvement
The Supreme Court ordered new elections
His cabinet voted him out of office
He lost the 1974 election in a landslide
questions.why: Lesson 3 says leaks to the Washington Post and then tapes provided the proof that ended his presidency in 1974.
